messages:
Nora: Tiny office debate: are YAML anchors secretly passive-aggressive? :thinking_face:
Kai: Yes. Theyre like, 'reuse me' but then you realize no one understands the alias chain. :exploding_head:
Evan: Semver would file a complaint: 'I was bumped without consent (v2.0.0)!' :page_with_curl:
linter-bot: LINT: detected duplicate anchors in configs/feature-flags.yaml: consider using explicit keys instead of &aliases
Nora: here's what started it all:
```yaml
defaults: &defaults
  timeout: 30
  retries: 2
feature_a:
  <<: *defaults
  retries: 3
feature_b:
  <<: *defaults
  timeout: 25
feature_c:
  <<: *defaults
  - unexpected_list_item: true
```
Kai: someone mixed a mapping and a list. classic anchor betrayal.
Evan: Proposal: Any PR that uses anchors must include a one-line explanation in the PR body. "Why this alias exists" kind of thing. Saves future archaeologists. :scroll:
Nora: I second. Also semver rule: if you drop a breaking change without a changelog, you owe the team coffee. Hot, not cold. :coffee:
linter-bot: :white_check_mark: rule added: anchors flagged for review if merging more than 3 hunks.
Kai: can we get an "Ask me about my YAML anchors" sticker? I'll wear it ironically.
Evan: and a matching sticker for semver: "I promise this major bump is important" :stuck_out_tongue_winking_eye:
Nora: vote on snacks for next standup if linter catches an anchor misuse: donuts vs bagels. Results?
Kai: donuts forever.
Evan: bagels for life.
Nora: tie. Team democratic snack outcome: bring both. Mission accomplished. :tada:
